From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: VPC Shield preflight: network inventory & next steps

Hi Alex / Sita —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and our recommended next steps so we can firm up whether FinSecure should go Hosted -> Dedicated -> Private VPC. Summary below:

1) Current ask: You want a fully private deployment (Private VPC) for production PII workloads, with strict egress controls and audit logging.
2) Scope we discussed: PrivateLink endpoint in us-west-2, customer-managed peering not preferred (you prefer endpoint-based flow), and a short blackout window for a cutover.
3) Key open items we need from your side to complete technical qualification:
   - Network inventory (subnets, NATs, firewall owners, firewall rules contact) — use the attached template.
   - Egress/ingress patterns for tokens to be allowed (outbound to Redwoods control plane & optional S3 endpoints).
   - KMS/HSM key owner contact for CMK integration.

Next steps / owners:
- Action (Alex): Fill and return the attached vpc_network_inventory_template.xlsx by EOD Friday (2027-08-27).
- Action (Ben): I’ll have Ben validate firewall rules and prepare a minimal allowlist for PrivateLink + console management.
- Action (Laura): I’ll loop Laura on compliance questions and SOC2 evidence/retention expectations.

Attachments: vpc_network_inventory_template.xlsx (xlsx) — please populate the yellow fields. Also attaching a short Redwood private deploy checklist for visibility.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-min network walkthrough next week (Ben + your network lead). Does Tues 8/31 10:00am PT work?

Thanks,
Marissa

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. We’re broadly aligned. A couple quick clarifications before we start filling the template:

- PrivateLink vs Peering: Our security team prefers endpoint-based PrivateLink for control-plane connections but will allow VPC peering for data-plane only if there is a clear egress IP allowlist. Could you confirm whether Redwood requires inbound IPs from our side or only accepts outgoing PrivateLink connections?

- KMS: We have a dedicated key in AWS KMS (account 987654321) but need to confirm whether Redwood needs CMK grants or whether we can rotate keys on our schedule.

- Can you put the minimal allowlist (IPs/ports) in the template or a separate stub so our infra folks can validate quickly?

We’ll aim to return the populated inventory by EOD Friday, but Sita may need another business day for approvals. If that’s an issue, tell us and we’ll prioritize.

Alex

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@finsecure.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC Shield preflight: network inventory & next steps

Alex —

Short answers to your questions from the infra side:

- Connection model: For Private VPC we recommend PrivateLink for control-plane management (outbound from your VPC to our endpoint) and either PrivateLink or VPC peering for data-plane depending on throughput. PrivateLink means your VPC initiates the connection to our endpoint — no inbound openings required on your firewall beyond standard egress.

- Allowlist: I attached a stub in-line here for the common minimal allowlist we need (replace X.Y.Z.0/24 placeholders with your egress CIDRs):

  Minimal allowlist for PrivateLink control plane:
  - outbound to endpoints: *.redwood-control.us-west-2.redwood.ai (443) -> allow egress to Redwood-managed endpoints
  - optional: S3 endpoints for model artifacts (if you want artifact pull via your VPC endpoint) -> s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com (443)
  - NTP/DNS egress as per your standard policy.

- KMS/CMK: We can operate with your CMK if you give the Redwood service principal a grant for encrypt/decrypt of the model keys. Rotation is supported; we’ll want notification pre-rotation or a brief maintenance window. I’ll follow up with a short CMK integration checklist.

I’m happy to take the network walkthrough once we have the inventory. If you want to speed things up, return the template with partial answers — we can iterate.

Ben

Appreciate the quick replies — thanks Alex and Ben. Finalizing action items here so everyone has a simple checklist:

1) Alex / Sita (FinSecure) — populate vpc_network_inventory_template.xlsx and return to marissa@redwood.ai by close of day Mon 2027-08-30 if EOD Friday is tight. Highlight unknown fields.
2) Ben (Redwood) — Circulate a short allowlist stub and CMK integration checklist by EOD today (attached as redwood_private_deploy_checklist.pdf).
3) Laura (Redwood) — Prepare SOC2 evidence overview and retention window doc for FinSecure; share any additional compliance asks they should include.
4) Schedule: Tentative network walkthrough on Tue 8/31 10:00am PT — Marissa will send a calendar invite if that time is good.

Open questions (for next call): preferred data-plane model (PrivateLink vs peering for bulk inference traffic), expected throughput (qps), and whether artifact pulls should use S3 via VPC endpoints or be proxied by Redwood. If you can include estimates in the template that helps us size Dedicated vs Private capacity.

Thanks — looking forward to the inventory.

Marissa
